1.s: Paul writes from prison to his friend Philemon about Onesimus, a runaway slave who became a Christian with Paul. He asks Philemon to receive him “no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a beloved brother,” and offers to pay any debt himself.
1.d: The name Onesimus means “useful”, and Paul plays on it. The letter reshapes relationships through the gospel; later Christians drew on it in the fight against slavery.
